confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches. Their results summarised crowd-sourced and modelled cost-of-living figures for Cairo, though I did not open the pages myself. Inexpensive meal: Wise about $5, Numbeo about $4.46, Hikersbay about $3.80. Mid-range meal for two: Wise about $28, Numbeo about $26.79. Cappuccino: about $1.68–1.80. Domestic draft beer: about $1.38–1.87. These sources disagree somewhat, and the Numbeo Cairo page in Egyptian pounds may be stale, so I used values in the middle of the range. The figures date from late 2026, and I used them as a stand-in for July 2026. The cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. They are based on summaries of aggregator figures (Expatistan about $5.65 for a cocktail and a nightlife guide about $4.60) and undated guide and hotel-menu ranges (cocktails EGP 180–500, local wine by the glass EGP 150–300). Alcohol is sold mainly in hotels and licensed bars, so prices vary widely by venue. The accommodation anchors are my own overall estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or current listings. Cairo hostel and budget hotel prices vary a lot by neighbourhood (Downtown vs Zamalek vs Giza) and season, so these are the least certain anchors. The FX rate is the RBA observation for 18 Nov 2026 as reported in a search result summary that cited the RBA's exchange rates page.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Cairo as a large, low-cost MENA capital with a weak local currency. It is broadly comparable to cities such as Amman (cheaper than Amman) or Tunis for restaurant prices. Alcohol is a licensed, venue-dependent premium item, similar to other Muslim-majority tourist hubs.
